[P1] 世界经典童话双语绘本
The Wild Swans
野天鹅
（丹麦）安徒生 著
外语教学与研究出版社
FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING AND RESEARCH PRESS

[P2] 萤火虫 世界经典童话双语绘本
The Wild Swans
野天鹅
（丹麦）安徒生 著
外语教学与研究出版社
FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING AND RESEARCH PRESS
北京 BEIJING

[P3] 从前，在一个遥远的地方，有一位国王，他的妻子虽然去世得早，但留下了十一个儿子和一个名叫艾丽莎的小女儿。这十二个孩子个个聪明又可爱，一家人相亲相爱，生活得非常幸福。
可是好景不长，几年后，国王和一个邪恶的女人结婚了。新王后不喜欢这些孩子，她尤其讨厌最小的艾丽莎。一天，国王带着王子们打猎去了，王后趁机把艾丽莎送到了乡下一个农夫的家里。

[P4] 王子们回来以后，发现小妹妹不见了，于是愤怒地去找王后要人。没想到王后对着他们念了一段咒语，把他们变成了十一只野天鹅。野天鹅发出悲伤的叫声，从窗户飞出了皇宫。当他们经过农夫的屋子时，艾丽莎正在熟睡中。他们并不知道他们的小妹妹就住在这里，所以他们并没有在这里停留，而是用力拍打着翅膀，飞进高高的云层，飞向遥远的大海。

[P5] 艾丽莎渐渐长大了，她出落得越来越美丽，就像清晨里一朵带着露水的玫瑰。
有一天，她和往常一样去森林里采浆果。在一条小河边，她遇见了一位老婆婆。老婆婆其实是一个好心的仙女，她告诉艾丽莎，她的哥哥们变成了野天鹅，已经飞到海边去了。
艾丽莎非常想念哥哥们，她下定决心，不管有多辛苦，都一定要找到他们。

[P6] 艾丽莎按照老婆婆的指示，日夜兼程，风餐露宿，终于来到了海边。
傍晚，十一只戴着金冠的野天鹅拍着白色的翅膀，缓缓地落到了地面上。当太阳刚从海平面上落下时，野天鹅就变成了十一位英俊的王子。
他们正是艾丽莎日夜思念的哥哥们。在白天，他们会变成野天鹅，只有太阳落山后他们才可以变回王子。
哥哥们告诉艾丽莎，第二天，他们就要飞越大海，飞往南方一个遥远的国家过冬了。艾丽莎希望和哥哥们一块儿去。

[P7] 夜里，王子们用芦苇织了一张结实的大网，让艾丽莎坐在网上。第二天，当太阳升起的时候，王子们又变成了野天鹅。他们用嘴衔起大网，飞向了大海的上空。
因为带着小妹妹，他们的飞行速度比平时慢得多。不知不觉已经到了傍晚，太阳在慢慢地下沉。如果再不降落到地上，哥哥们就会恢复人形，大家都会掉到海里淹死。艾丽莎不由得焦急万分。
就在这时，前方出现了一块陆地，野天鹅马上朝着陆地飞去。终于，大家赶在太阳落山之前安全着陆了。

[P8] 艾丽莎和哥哥们在一片美丽的森林里安了家。
一天夜里，艾丽莎梦见了那位仙女婆婆。她告诉艾丽莎，只要采来森林里的荨麻，织成十一件披肩给王子们穿上，咒语就可以解除。不过，在披肩织好以前，艾丽莎不能说话，否则王子们就会死去。
仙女婆婆说完，递给艾丽莎一束荨麻。艾丽莎一摸到粗糙、刺手的荨麻，就疼得从梦里惊醒过来。

[P9] 艾丽莎马上走出山洞，采来荨麻，光着脚把它们踩碎，再搓成绿色的线。她的手脚被荨麻扎得火辣辣地痛，还变得又红又肿，但一想到能解除哥哥们的咒语，艾丽莎就什么痛苦都不怕了。
太阳下山后，哥哥们回来了。他们看到艾丽莎一言不发，手脚被刺得又红又肿，就知道她是在为他们受苦。最小的哥哥忍不住哭了起来，神奇的是，当他的泪珠滴到艾丽莎的手上，那里的红肿就立刻消失了。

[P10] 第二天，哥哥们变成野天鹅飞走后，森林里响起了号角声。一群打猎的骑士来到了艾丽莎面前，他们中间最英武的那位就是这个国家的国王。
国王喜欢上了沉默而美丽的艾丽莎，他不仅把艾丽莎带进了皇宫，还为她准备了一间漂亮的卧室。但是，国王的叔叔不喜欢总抱着荨麻的艾丽莎，他认为艾丽莎一定是一个用巫术迷住国王的巫婆。

[P11] 而艾丽莎也渐渐爱上了温柔体贴的国王，可她仍然不能说话，而且每天都要不停地编织披肩。当她织完第七件披肩的时候，荨麻用完了。皇宫后面有一片可怕的黑森林，那里长着许多荨麻。在一个月光明亮的夜里，艾丽莎勇敢地走进黑森林去采集荨麻。
这一切都被国王的叔叔看在眼里。传说中只有巫婆才敢在晚上走进黑森林，于是，他更加肯定艾丽莎是一个巫婆了。

[P12] 国王的叔叔把看到的情景告诉了国王。从那以后，国王再也睡不好了。他怎么也不能相信，自己深爱的姑娘竟然是个可怕的巫婆，但自己的叔叔总不可能说谎吧。
就在最后一件披肩即将完工时，荨麻又用完了，艾丽莎不得不再次冒险去摘荨麻。国王悄悄地跟在艾丽莎身后，亲眼看着她走进黑森林。国王终于相信了叔叔的话，他擦掉脸上的泪水，命令卫兵把艾丽莎关进监狱。

[P13] 监狱里又阴冷又潮湿，艾丽莎没有枕头和被子，只能把头枕在荨麻上面，把粗硬的披肩盖在身上。
在这个国家里，巫婆是要被烧死的。监狱看守偷偷告诉艾丽莎，国王已经下令，三天之后处决她。可是为了哥哥们，艾丽莎什么也不怕，她只想赶在三天之内织好最后一件披肩，解除哥哥们身上的咒语。
艾丽莎夜以继日地工作。小老鼠帮助她把荨麻拖到脚下，画眉鸟陪伴在她的左右，用动听的歌声鼓励她。

[P14] 三天很快就过去了。黄昏时分，监狱窗外响起了野天鹅扇动翅膀的声音。丽莎向外望去，原来是哥哥们来了，她快乐得呜咽起来。
晚上，王子们来到皇宫，想把事情的真相告诉国王，可是，伤心的国王早已休息了，卫兵不让他们进去。王子们和卫兵起了冲突。终于，国王被吵醒了，但就在此时，太阳从天边升了起来，王子们又变回了野天鹅。

[P15] 卫兵将艾丽莎拖上马车，马车载着她向刑场驶去。可她还在不停地编织着。只差一点儿就能织完最后一件披肩了！
看热闹的人们都听信国王叔叔的话，认为艾丽莎是巫婆，认为她手中的荨麻披肩是邪恶的象征。大家都对她指指点点，恶言相向。这时，十一只野天鹅从天而降，它们落到马车上，张开宽大的翅膀，保护着艾丽莎。

[P16] 刑场到了，卫兵们抓住艾丽莎，要把她拖下车。这时，艾丽莎终于织完了最后一件披肩，她急忙把十一件披肩抛向天空。转眼间，穿上披肩的野天鹅变成了十一位英俊的王子。
艾丽莎终于可以说话了，她把事情的真相告诉了国王。她话音刚落，地上就长出了许多红玫瑰。国王摘下一朵玫瑰，插在艾丽莎的头上，并请她做自己的新娘。在哥哥们的衷心祝福下，艾丽莎与国王结为夫妻，从此过上了幸福的生活。
full_text_en:
[P1] World Classic Fairy Tale Bilingual Picture Book
The Wild Swans
Wild Swans
By Hans Christian Andersen (Denmark)
Foreign Language Teaching and Research Press
FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING AND RESEARCH PRESS

[P2] Firefly World Classic Fairy Tale Bilingual Picture Book
The Wild Swans
Wild Swans
By Hans Christian Andersen (Denmark)
Foreign Language Teaching and Research Press
Beijing BEIJING

[P3] Once upon a time, in a distant land, there was a king. His wife had died young, leaving behind eleven sons and a little daughter named Elisa. These twelve children were all clever and lovely, and the family loved each other dearly, living a very happy life.
But happiness did not last long. A few years later, the king married an evil woman. The new queen disliked the children, and she especially hated the youngest, Elisa. One day, when the king took the princes hunting, the queen took the opportunity to send Elisa to the home of a farmer in the countryside.

[P4] After the princes returned, they found their little sister was missing, so they angrily went to the queen to demand an explanation. Unexpectedly, the queen recited a spell over them, turning them into eleven wild swans. The swans let out sorrowful cries and flew out of the palace windows. As they passed by the farmer's house, Elisa was fast asleep. They did not know their little sister lived there, so they did not stop. Instead, they flapped their wings hard, flying into the high clouds and toward the distant sea.

[P5] Elisa grew up, and she became more and more beautiful, like a rose in the morning with dew.
One day, she went to the forest to pick berries as usual. By a small river, she met an old woman. The old woman was actually a kind fairy, who told Elisa that her brothers had turned into wild swans and had flown to the seaside.
Elisa missed her brothers very much. She made up her mind that no matter how hard it was, she would definitely find them.

[P6] Elisa followed the old woman's instructions, traveling day and night, enduring wind and rain, and finally arrived at the seaside.
In the evening, eleven wild swans wearing golden crowns flapped their white wings and slowly landed on the ground. When the sun just set below the horizon, the swans turned into eleven handsome princes.
They were exactly the brothers Elisa had longed for day and night. During the day, they turned into wild swans, and only after the sun set could they return to their prince forms.
The brothers told Elisa that the next day, they would fly across the sea to a distant southern country for the winter. Elisa hoped to go with her brothers.

[P7] At night, the princes wove a sturdy net from reeds and placed Elisa on it. The next day, when the sun rose, the princes turned back into wild swans. They carried the net with their beaks and flew into the sky above the sea.
Because they were carrying their little sister, their flying speed was much slower than usual. Before they knew it, it was already evening, and the sun was slowly setting. If they didn't land on the ground soon, the brothers would revert to human form, and everyone would fall into the sea and drown. Elisa became extremely anxious.
Just then, a piece of land appeared ahead, and the wild swans immediately flew toward it. Finally, everyone landed safely before the sun set.

[P8] Elisa and her brothers settled in a beautiful forest.
One night, Elisa dreamed of the fairy grandmother. She told Elisa that if she picked nettle from the forest and wove eleven shawls for the princes to wear, the spell could be lifted. However, before the shawls were finished, Elisa could not speak, or the princes would die.
After the fairy grandmother finished speaking, she handed Elisa a bundle of nettle. Elisa, upon touching the rough, prickly nettle, woke up from her dream in pain.

[P9] Elisa immediately left the cave, picked nettle, crushed them barefoot, and then twisted them into green thread. Her hands and feet stung fiercely from the nettles, turning red and swollen, but thinking of breaking the curse on her brothers, Elisa feared no pain.
After the sun set, her brothers returned. Seeing Elisa silent, with her hands and feet red and swollen from the stings, they knew she was suffering for them. The youngest brother couldn't help but cry. Miraculously, when his tear fell onto Elisa's hand, the redness and swelling vanished instantly.

[P10] The next day, after the brothers had flown away as wild swans, horns sounded in the forest. A group of hunting knights arrived before Elisa, and the most valiant among them was the king of this country.
The king fell in love with the silent and beautiful Elisa. He not only brought her into the palace but also prepared a lovely bedroom for her. However, the king's uncle disliked Elisa, who was always holding nettle, and thought she must be a witch who had enchanted the king with magic.

[P11] Elisa gradually fell in love with the gentle and kind king, but she still couldn't speak, and every day she had to keep weaving shawls. When she finished weaving the seventh shawl, the nettle was all used up. Behind the palace was a terrifying dark forest, where many nettles grew. On a bright moonlit night, Elisa bravely walked into the dark forest to collect nettles.
All of this was seen by the king's uncle. It was said that only witches dared to enter the dark forest at night, so he became even more certain that Elisa was a witch.

[P12] The king's uncle told the king what he had seen. From then on, the king couldn't sleep. He couldn't believe that the girl he loved was a terrible witch, but his uncle couldn't possibly be lying.
Just as the last shawl was about to be finished, the nettle ran out again, and Elisa had to risk going out to pick more. The king secretly followed Elisa and watched her enter the dark forest. The king finally believed his uncle's words. He wiped the tears from his face and ordered the guards to lock Elisa in prison.

[P13] The prison was cold and damp. Elisa had no pillow or blanket, so she had to rest her head on nettles and cover herself with a rough shawl.
In this country, witches were to be burned. The prison guard secretly told Elisa that the king had ordered her execution in three days. But for her brothers, Elisa feared nothing. She only wanted to finish weaving the last shawl within three days to break the curse on her brothers.
Elisa worked day and night. Little mice helped her drag the nettles to her feet, and the thrush stayed by her side, encouraging her with its beautiful song.

[P14] Three days passed quickly. At dusk, the sound of wild swans flapping their wings rang out outside the prison window. Lisa looked out and saw her brothers had arrived; she wept with joy.
That night, the princes came to the palace, wanting to tell the king the truth. But the sorrowful king had already gone to sleep, and the guards would not let them in. The princes clashed with the guards. Finally, the king was awakened, but at that very moment, the sun rose over the horizon, and the princes turned back into wild swans.

[P15] The soldiers dragged Elisa onto the cart, and the cart carried her toward the execution ground. But she was still weaving tirelessly. She was just a little bit away from finishing the last shawl!
Onlookers believed the king's uncle and thought Elisa was a witch, believing the nettle shawl in her hands was a symbol of evil. Everyone pointed fingers and spoke ill of her. At that moment, eleven wild swans descended from the sky. They landed on the cart, spreading their broad wings to protect Elisa.

[P16] The execution ground had arrived, and the soldiers grabbed Elisa, trying to drag her off the cart. At that moment, Elisa had finally finished weaving the last shawl. She hurriedly threw the eleven shawls into the sky. In an instant, the wild swans wearing the shawls turned into eleven handsome princes.
Elisa could finally speak. She told the king the truth. As soon as her words fell, many red roses sprouted from the ground. The king picked a rose and placed it on Elisa's head, asking her to be his bride. With her brothers' heartfelt blessings, Elisa married the king and lived happily ever after.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《野天鹅》的封面，展示了女主角被一群天鹅环绕的插画，上方有中英文书名及作者信息，下方为出版社名称。
[P2] 本页为绘本《野天鹅》的封面，展示了书名、作者（丹麦）安徒生及出版社信息，插画中有一对男女角色和城堡背景。
[P3] 本页讲述了《野天鹅》故事的开端：国王与前妻育有十二个孩子，生活幸福；但新王后嫉妒并厌恶最小的女儿艾丽莎，趁国王外出打猎时，将她送往乡下农夫家。
[P4] 王子们发现妹妹艾丽莎失踪后去找王后，却被王后用咒语变成十一只野天鹅，他们悲伤地飞离皇宫，经过农夫家时未发现熟睡的艾丽莎，继续飞向大海。
[P5] 艾丽莎在采浆果时遇见一位好心的仙女，得知哥哥们已变成野天鹅飞往海边，她决心无论如何都要找到他们。
[P6] 艾丽莎历经艰辛来到海边，终于找到了变成野天鹅的哥哥们。在太阳落山后，哥哥们变回王子，告诉艾丽莎他们即将飞往南方过冬，艾丽莎希望能与他们同行。
[P7] 王子们用芦苇网带着艾丽莎飞向大海，因飞行速度变慢而面临太阳落山前无法降落的危险，最终在日落前发现陆地并安全着陆。
[P8] 艾丽莎和哥哥们在森林里安家，她梦见仙女婆婆告诉她，必须用荨麻织成十一件披肩才能解除哥哥们的咒语，但在此期间她不能说话，否则哥哥们会死去。艾丽莎从梦中惊醒，感受到荨麻的刺痛。
[P9] 艾丽莎为了解除哥哥们的咒语，忍痛采集荨麻并搓成线，哥哥们归来后看到她受伤，最小的哥哥流泪，泪水奇迹般治好了她的红肿。
[P10] 艾丽莎被国王带回皇宫，国王为她准备了卧室，但国王的叔叔怀疑她是用巫术迷惑国王的巫婆。
[P11] 艾丽莎为织披肩采集荨麻，夜晚独自进入黑森林，国王的叔叔因此更加怀疑她是巫婆。
[P12] 国王的叔叔告知国王艾丽莎夜间进入黑森林，国王虽心存怀疑，但最终相信了叔叔的话，下令将艾丽莎关进监狱。
[P13] 艾丽莎被关进阴冷潮湿的监狱，面临三天后被处决的命运。她不顾危险，夜以继日地用荨麻织披肩，小老鼠和画眉鸟陪伴并帮助她。
[P14] 三天期限将至，艾丽莎在监狱中听到哥哥们化作野天鹅飞来的声响，她激动落泪。当晚，哥哥们试图向国王说明真相，但国王已睡，卫兵阻拦，冲突中国王被吵醒，然而太阳升起，哥哥们再次变回野天鹅。
[P15] 艾丽莎被押往刑场，仍在坚持编织最后一件披肩，围观人群因国王叔叔的挑拨而对她恶语相向，此时十一只野天鹅从天而降，飞落马车，展开翅膀保护她。
[P16] 艾丽莎在刑场抛出最后一件披肩，十一只野天鹅变回王子，她终于能说话并说出真相，国王被感动，将她迎娶为妻，众人在玫瑰花丛中幸福团聚。
[P17] 画面中，一位头戴王冠、身着王子服饰的少年长着洁白的翅膀，在浅绿色的天空中飞翔，周围有细小的光点飘散，象征着魔法或转变的瞬间。
